summit.title: Walls, roofs and the sea
summit.story: Dubrovnik's grand tables use the fortifications as their dining rooms, and most of them keep a summer calendar. Restaurant 360 is built into the casemates of the wall above the Old Port and is the city's only MICHELIN-starred table in 2026, with Gault&Millau giving Marijo Curić's kitchen 18/20. Stara Loža climbs through a fifteenth-century Prijeko townhouse to a small rooftop and is in the MICHELIN selection in 2026. Nautika, outside the Pile Gate, occupies the 1881 school of navigation, looks across at Lovrijenac, and scores 16.5/20 with Gault&Millau in 2026. Late in October the two seasonal houses are at or past the end of their season, so call before you book.
summit.where: Restaurant 360, Old Port; Stara Loža, Prijeko; Nautika, Pile

houses.title: Old kitchens inside the walls
houses.story: Inside the walls the old houses cook the city's own food, though Croatia Week reports that nearly all of the centre's places close in winter. Proto has grilled fish off the Stradun since 1886, scores 14.5/20 with Gault&Millau in 2026, and keeps a winter schedule. Kopun, on the Jesuit square, is built around one Renaissance-era dish, capon with orange and honey, and earns 86 Falstaff points in 2026. Lady Pi-Pi is the counterpoint: a charcoal grill under a vine roof near the north wall that takes no bookings and works from April to mid October; it is closed now until Easter. City rules from 2024 push terrace users to trade at least one winter month.
houses.where: Proto, Široka; Kopun, Poljana Ruđera Boškovića; Lady Pi-Pi, Peline

konoba.title: Under the iron bell
konoba.story: Out of town the konoba cooks under the peka, an iron bell heaped with embers over meat or octopus and potatoes, and the dish has to be ordered by phone hours in advance. Konoba Dubrava, a family house in Bosanka on Srđ ten minutes above the walls, asks for three to four hours' notice for lamb, veal or octopus. Konavoski Dvori, in a restored watermill on the cold Ljuta river in Konavle, adds the valley's own dishes: river trout and frogs stewed in brodet, served by staff in Konavle costume. Neither published 2026 dates or winter hours in what we found, so the phone call that orders the peka also confirms the table.
konoba.where: Konoba Dubrava, Bosanka; Konavoski Dvori, Ljuta

oysters.title: Oysters at the source
oysters.story: The European flat oyster, Ostrea edulis, has been farmed in the bay below Ston's walls for centuries, and the restaurants of Mali Ston serve it a few metres from the beds, an hour north of Dubrovnik. Bota Šare was opened by Božidar 'Bota' Šare and his wife Tanja in a vaulted old salt store; the family name now runs oyster and sushi bars in Dubrovnik, Split and Zagreb, all supplied from Mali Ston. Vila Koruna, serving since 1973, keeps its shellfish in seawater tanks on the terrace and offers oysters eleven ways. Older listings say the Mali Ston houses work through the winter, but neither published 2026 winter hours.
oysters.where: Bota Šare, Mali Ston; Vila Koruna, Mali Ston

locals.title: Where Dubrovnik eats off-stage
locals.story: When the cruise crowds fill the Stradun, the city eats a few streets away, where the menus are not written in eight languages. Taj Mahal, on Nikole Gučetića inside the walls, is a Bosnian family house with a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, meat from its own butcher and a plum baklava made by the owner's mother. Pizzeria Tabasco, on Hvarska above the Ploče gate, fires its pizzas in a wood oven and is listed open most of the year, with shorter winter hours. Neither is about the sea view; both are about price and appetite, and both are a short walk from the walls.
locals.where: Taj Mahal, Old Town; Pizzeria Tabasco, Ploče; Atlantic Kitchen, Lapad

glass.title: Plavac Mali and Pošip
glass.story: South Dalmatia's wine comes mostly from the Pelješac peninsula, an hour north of Dubrovnik, and its red grape is Plavac Mali. Grgić Vina at Trstenik, founded in 1996 by Mike Grgich after his Paris win of 1976, makes just two wines; Falstaff scored both 93 in April 2026. Vinarija Miloš at Ponikve, near Ston, ages its Stagnum in old Slavonian oak, and Falstaff gave the 2016 a 94 the same month. In the Old Town, D'vino on Palmotićeva pours more than 60 Croatian wines by the glass, though it keeps tourist-season months.
glass.where: D'vino, Dubrovnik Old Town; Grgić Vina, Trstenik; Vinarija Miloš, Ponikve

street.title: The market and the bun
street.story: Dubrovnik's cheap food starts at the Gruž market on the harbour, where Time Out says fish from the Elafiti islands is best before seven and Friday and Saturday are the busiest days. Inside the walls, Buffet Škola on Antuninska fills house-baked bread with Drniš pršut and Konavle cheese, and made both Gault&Millau and Falstaff in 2026. Barba, on Boškovićeva, turns octopus, anchovies and shrimp into burgers and sandwiches eaten standing in the lane. The fish hall is cash only, and buying there means cooking on board or handing the bag to a galley. All three are quick, and none takes bookings.
street.where: Gruž Market, Gruž; Buffet Škola, Old Town; Barba, Old Town
